children: Wall Street ended October with a sell-off

lost over 40% of its value in October alone, its worst month since 1974, after weaker-than-expected guidance. More than 10 chip stocks fell by over 20% on the month, with Friday’s sell-off wiping out $1 trillion of market value across the sector.
A new week of earnings kicks off with the focus on tech mega caps.
on Nov. 4, both after the close. AMD and Qualcomm each fell more than 11% on Friday.

Yet, the biggest expected swings are elsewhere. Ten stocks with a market cap of at least $25 billion are priced for moves above 10%, and five of them are tech names that fell between 8.3% and 13.7% on Friday, according to
An implied move is the percentage swing in either direction that options traders expect right after earnings.
Which Stocks Could Swing The Most This Week?
The South Korea-focused e-commerce company reports Nov. 3 after the close. Analysts expect a loss of 3 cents per share on revenue of $9.70 billion.
Second-quarter revenue of $8.90 billion fell just short of estimates, and the shares dropped 4.6% the next day. Deutsche Bank upgraded the stock to Buy afterward.
The RAS-focused cancer drug developer reports Nov. 4 after the close. Consensus calls for a loss of $2.40 per share on revenue of $25.48 million.
On Oct. 15, European regulators’ CHMP recommended authorization for Rasonque in metastatic pancreatic cancer. TD Cowen reiterated Buy with a $250 target on Oct. 21.
The web infrastructure and security company reports Nov. 5 after the close. The Street expects earnings of 34 cents per share, in line with guidance, on revenue of $737.95 million.
The shares rose 5.6% after the second-quarter report. They fell 11.9% on Friday. Bernstein raised its target to $245 on Oct. 29 but kept Market Perform.
The genetic testing company reports Nov. 5 after the close. Analysts model a loss of 29 cents per share on revenue of $704.90 million.
The shares jumped 21.4% after the second-quarter report. On Oct. 27, Natera presented new Signatera data in bladder cancer, and BTIG raised its target to $430.
The optical components maker reports its fiscal first quarter Nov. 5 after the close. Consensus calls for earnings of $4.19 per share on revenue of $1.25 billion.

, according to Benzinga, then fell 11.1% on Friday. Jefferies raised its target to $1,250.
The cloud monitoring platform reports Nov. 4 before the open. Analysts expect earnings of 65 cents per share, the top of guidance, on revenue of $1.15 billion.
In August, earnings beat estimates, yet the shares fell 19.0%. They closed at $229.29 that day and traded near $229 on Friday.
The medical supplies maker, public since December 2025, reports Nov. 4 before the open. The Street expects earnings of 35 cents per share on revenue of $7.72 billion.
The shares fell 12.8% after a second-quarter beat. On Oct. 21, the company announced the exit of Medline-brand beds, with costs up to $220 million, according to Benzinga.
The optical networking components maker reports its fiscal first quarter Nov. 4 after the close. Analysts model earnings of $1.97 per share on revenue of $2.31 billion.
The shares fell 8.0% after the last report and 12.7% on Friday. B. Riley lowered its target to $262 on Oct. 30.
The mobile advertising technology company reports Nov. 4 after the close. Consensus calls for earnings of $4.04 per share on revenue of $2.08 billion.
The shares fell 19.7% after the last report and hit 52-week lows in October, according to Benzinga. UBS and RBC Capital lowered their targets on Oct. 28.
The mRNA company reports Nov. 6 before the open. Analysts expect a loss of $1.25 per share on revenue of $885.05 million.

On Oct. 22, Merck and Moderna reported Phase 3 melanoma data showing a 42% lower risk of recurrence or death, and the shares plunged about 15% after a YouTuber disclosed a put position, according to Benzinga. William Blair downgraded the stock on Oct. 27.
